history: High white blood cell count reported 2 years ago

diagnostic_test.name: Hematologic and Imaging Workup with Biopsies
procedure: Complete blood cell count and peripheral blood smear
Interphase fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for FIP1L1::PDGFRA rearrangement
findings: 55% eosinophils with absolute eosinophil count of 12,290/μL
Bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow (100% cellularity) with myeloid hyperplasia, increased eosinophils with dysplasia, and 2% blasts
PET/CT scan revealing a left upper cervical lymph node of 2.6 cm and a left inguinal lymph node of 3.1 × 2.3 cm with an SUV max of 5.7
Lymph node biopsy showing partial involvement by atypical cells with a high proliferation index (Ki-67 >95%) positive for CD3, CD4, CD8, BCL2, and TDT

branch.interpretation: Integration of clinical history, laboratory data, imaging, and pathology findings to determine the neoplastic process.
branch.result: The presence of marked eosinophilia, myeloid hyperplasia, and the FIP1L1::PDGFRA rearrangement, along with a lymph node biopsy showing a T-cell immunophenotype, suggests a neoplasm that bridges myeloid and lymphoid features.

diagnostic_options.description: A benign inflammatory disorder typically presenting with painless lymphadenopathy and eosinophilia.
evidence_against: Marked leukocytosis and bone marrow changes
High proliferation index and T-cell marker positivity

diagnostic_options.description: A lymphoma characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells and a typical immunophenotypic profile.
evidence_against: Immunohistochemical profile inconsistent with Hodgkin lymphoma
Marked eosinophilia and myeloid hyperplasia not typical for Hodgkin lymphoma

diagnostic_options.description: A neoplasm of lymphoblasts with T-cell lineage markers and high proliferative index.
evidence_against: Bone marrow findings of myeloid hyperplasia and marked eosinophilia
Presence of significant FIP1L1::PDGFRA rearrangement which is not typical for isolated T-cell ALL

diagnostic_options.option: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions
diagnostic_options.description: A neoplasm characterized by features of both myeloid and lymphoid proliferation associated with genetic rearrangements such as FIP1L1::PDGFRA.
evidence_for: Bone marrow hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia
Lymph node involvement with atypical T-cell phenotype suggesting a lymphoblastic component
evidence_against: T-cell markers might initially suggest a pure lymphoblastic process, but they can be part of the transformation in this neoplasm

conclusion: The overall findings support the diagnosis of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions.
